original_statement.verbatim_html:
First consider K particles performing independent Brownian motion on the positive half-line, with state 0 absorbing, and each particle started at state 1 at time 0. Now suppose we have at our disposal a unit quantity of positive drift, which we can distribute amongst the non-absorbed particles at time t according to any control policy we choose. Let F(K) be the maximum, over all control policies, of the expectation of the number of particles that survive forever.

It is a challenging exercise in stochastic calculus to show that F(K) grows as order K^{1/2}.

Problem. Prove F(K) = (c + o(1))K^{1/2} for some explicit constant c.

Problem. Analyze the policy of assigning drift 1 to the leftmost particle.
